before.definition: Reading pages in the order they are stored. The storage and the operating system can read ahead, so each page is cheaper than with random I/O. PostgreSQL charges seq_page_cost (default 1.0) per page.

after.definition: Reading pages in their stored order, often allowing storage and the operating system to read ahead. PostgreSQL models sequential page fetches with seq_page_cost, default 1.0; actual access cost depends on storage and cache state.

corrections.reason: Independent primary-source correction of an overbroad or mismatched meaning.

before.definition: The Oversized-Attribute Storage Technique: PostgreSQL stores large values (long text, big JSON) compressed or in a separate table, fetching them only when a query asks for that column.

after.definition: The Oversized-Attribute Storage Technique: PostgreSQL can compress large column values or store them out of line in a separate table. Fetching or decompressing those values can be deferred until an operation needs their contents.

corrections.reason: Independent primary-source correction of an overbroad or mismatched meaning.

before.definition: When a bitmap is too big for work_mem, PostgreSQL remembers only which pages match, not which rows (lossy), and must recheck the condition on every row of those pages (Recheck Cond).

after.definition: Lossy bitmap pages retain page locations rather than individual tuple locations, so the heap scan must recheck candidate rows. Memory pressure can cause lossification, while some index methods are inherently lossy; a displayed Recheck Cond alone does not prove either cause.

corrections.reason: Independent primary-source correction of an overbroad or mismatched meaning.

before.definition: Paging with LIMIT n OFFSET k. The database must produce and throw away all k skipped rows, so later pages get steadily slower.
before.example: OFFSET 900000 walked 900,020 index entries to return 20 rows.

after.definition: Paging with LIMIT and OFFSET. PostgreSQL must compute the skipped rows as well as the returned rows, so a large offset can add substantial work; actual latency depends on the plan, filters and cache state.
after.example: OFFSET 900000 walked 900,020 index entries to return 20 rows.

corrections.reason: Independent primary-source correction of an overbroad or mismatched meaning.

before.definition: A holding table used to load and prepare data before it moves into its final tables. A staging environment is a separate system used to test changes before deployment; these are distinct uses of staging.

after.definition: A separate system used to test changes before deploying them to production. A staging table instead holds data during a load or transformation; these are distinct meanings of staging.

corrections.reason: Independent primary-source correction of an overbroad or mismatched meaning.

before.definition: Comma-separated values: a plain-text table format with one row per line and commas between fields.

after.definition: Comma-separated values: a plain-text format with comma-separated fields. Records are normally separated by line breaks, but quoted fields may themselves contain commas, quotes or line breaks.

corrections.reason: Independent primary-source correction of an overbroad or mismatched meaning.

before.definition: In PostgreSQL, the main storage of a table: its rows kept in pages in no particular order. An index stores only keys and row pointers, so an index scan usually has to fetch each matching row from the heap.

after.definition: PostgreSQL’s main table storage, holding physical row versions in pages without a guaranteed logical row order. Standard builds use 8 KiB pages; page size is selected at build time. after.definition: Work that keeps an index consistent with table changes and reclaims obsolete entries. INSERT and relevant non-HOT UPDATE operations can add entries; partial indexes hold only rows satisfying their predicate, HOT can avoid new ordinary index entries, and obsolete entries may be reclaimed later, for example by VACUUM. Summarising indexes such as BRIN have their own maintenance rules.
after.example: Changing an INCLUDE value in a B-tree can prevent HOT and require new ordinary index entries. Inserting a row outside a partial index’s predicate adds no entry to that index.

corrections: V1 qp-hash-partition-io: 'If many rows share a key ... some partitions are too big and must be partitioned again' implied repartitioning fixes key skew. Rehashing cannot split rows that share one join-key value (PostgreSQL nodeHash.c disables further nbatch growth and lets the batch exceed its budget) -> body now says repartitioning helps only for a badly spread hash, and a single very common key must be joined another way or allowed to exceed memory; analogy limit and takeaway updated.

V2 qp-join-variants: 'the hash join (8 batches, 587 ms) beat a merge join that had to sort 3 million rows' was presented as a general result, but in the module's own dataset (order_items(order_id) index present) PostgreSQL 18.6 merge-joined two index scans with no sort and finished faster (768 vs 818 ms) though estimated costlier -> reframed as one illustrative run without that index, with a caveat that an index can remove the sort and change the comparison.

V3 qp-external-join-io-q1 option 3 explanation: 'only possible when one input fits in memory for an in-memory hash join' -> 'needs one input to fit in memory, as in an in-memory hash join' (a block nested loop with one input in memory also reads each table once).
V4 qp-index-page-selectivity: 'the index halved the time' for 23 ms vs 9.3 ms (less than half) -> 'the bitmap scan took well under half the time', labelled as an illustrative run.

H1 (hedge, not an error) illustrative-run labels added to single-run figures: qp-pull-and-blocking LIMIT 5 (85 rows/2 pages are position-dependent; my run read 354 rows/7 pages), qp-hash-join-mechanics 16% spill slowdown (27% in my run), qp-composite-index-order '2,400 descents' (2,401 here), qp-plan-operators 47 ms, qp-sargable-predicates 7.6x, qp-subquery-semantics 4x, qp-covering-partial-indexes 25x.

qp-query-round-trips.rationale: BitmapOr and the unindexed OR Seq Scan executed. t_total reference card recomputed (12,501 x 0.55 ms = 6.9 s, 6.25 s network). Shopping-trip analogy maps round trips; limit (batch size) accurate. q6 rewrite recomputed (2,001 x 0.4 ms = 0.8 s; 0.1 s execution).

questionsRewritten.qp-anti-patterns-q6: Rewritten from computing total wait to diagnosing N+1 and choosing the fix; 0.8 s network vs 0.1 s execution recomputed. Answer index 1.

qp-generic-plans-counts.rationale: Author correction confirmed against plancache.c choose_custom_plan (five custom plans, then generic only if cheaper than the average custom cost including a planning charge) and executed in 18.6: five 'pending' calls -> 6 then 7 and 9 custom, 0 generic (custom cost 657 vs generic 20,833); five 'shipped' calls (custom 22,250) -> generic chosen on the sixth call and reused for 'pending' (4 generic). force_custom_plan restores the partial-index plan. count(*) scan, CTE inlining since 12 executed/checked. Courier analogy and limit accurate.

questionsRewritten.qp-anti-patterns-q9: Factual correction confirmed: plancache.c keeps custom plans when they are cheaper than the generic plan, and PostgreSQL 18.6 kept custom plans after five 'pending' calls but switched to the reused generic Seq Scan after five 'shipped' calls. Scenario rewritten to the second case. Answer index 3.

qp-query-pipeline.rationale: Restaurant order: legibility check = parser, menu check = analyser, set-menu expansion = rewriter/view expansion, head chef = planner, cooks = executor. Limit (statistics-based estimates; rows stream rather than courses) is accurate.

qp-plan-operators.rationale: Recipe = logical SQL, cook's method = physical plan that may reorder steps. Limit (PostgreSQL does not switch algorithms mid-execution) is accurate.

qp-pull-and-blocking.rationale: Sandwich counter = next() pull chain stopped by LIMIT; teacher ranking papers = blocking Sort/HashAggregate. Limit (one process calls operators in turn; some engines push batches) is accurate.

qp-page-costs.rationale: Short factual unit on pages, hits and reads; the plain explanation is already concrete and an analogy would add length without insight.

qp-execution-models.rationale: Carrying tins one at a time vs a box = per-call overhead vs vectorised batch; friend = parallel worker. Limit (no storage saving; oversized batches lose cache benefit) is accurate.

qp-nested-loop-mechanics.rationale: Host reading the whole guest list per guest = plain nested loop; alphabetised list = index probe. Limit (Memoize is the only reuse; probes cost page reads) is accurate.

qp-hash-join-mechanics.rationale: Cloakroom hooks = build phase hash table; tickets = probes; rack complete before collection = blocking build. Limit (many matches per key; spilling to batches) is accurate.

qp-merge-join-mechanics.rationale: Two fingers down sorted register and test pile = merge positions. Limit (sorting cost if unsorted; duplicate groups need revisiting) is accurate.

qp-nested-loop-io.rationale: Textbook I/O counting procedure; the formula's In words line and worked orientation comparison already carry the intuition.

qp-external-join-io.rationale: Pass-counting procedure shown as a step table; an analogy would repeat it.

qp-hash-partition-io.rationale: Pigeonholes by surname = hash partitions; one pigeonhole at a time = per-partition join. I extended the limit: skew can overflow a pigeonhole, and one surname shared by half the post cannot be split by any re-sorting (single hot key; PostgreSQL nodeHash.c stops adding batches).

qp-join-choice.rationale: The crossover is clearest from the two cost shapes and the toy numbers; an analogy would add little.

qp-join-variants.rationale: Comparison table and plan-name vocabulary; earlier join lessons already carry analogies.

qp-column-statistics.rationale: Opinion poll = sampled ANALYZE; party shares = MCV frequencies; out-of-date poll = stale statistics. Limit (a table could be counted exactly but it would cost too much) is accurate.

qp-equality-selectivity.rationale: Remembered common surnames = MCV list; even share of the rest = residual rule; no common names = 1/n_distinct. Limit (sampled at last ANALYZE, refreshed by the database) is accurate.

qp-selectivity-dependencies.rationale: Welsh-and-speaks-Welsh guess = multiplied selectivities under independence; arithmetic 1/20 x 1/100 = 1/2,000 vs about 1/100 (20x too low) recomputed. Framed as a hypothetical stadium; proportions are rough and UK-like (Census 2021: 538,300 Welsh speakers aged 3+, 17.8% of Wales). Limit (planner sees only collected statistics until extended statistics exist) is accurate.

qp-estimates-and-costs.rationale: Default-selectivity and cost-parameter tables with worked sums; an analogy would not clarify the arithmetic.

qp-join-search.rationale: Delivery round: best plan per group of stops reused = dynamic programming over subsets; trial-and-improvement route = GEQO. Limit (costs rest on estimates) is accurate.

qp-refresh-statistics.rationale: Sat-nav with an old map = planner with pre-load statistics; updating the map = ANALYZE. Limit (no mid-query replanning) is accurate.

qp-explain-fields.rationale: Field-by-field reference for EXPLAIN output; an analogy would not help read the fields.

qp-explain-loops.rationale: Three reading rules best taught on real plan excerpts with the subtraction and multiplication shown.

qp-explain-access.rationale: Red-flags checklist and plan excerpts; diagnostic content, not a mechanism needing a comparison.

qp-explain-buffers.rationale: Buffer-counter definitions and an investigation method; concrete already.

qp-index-page-selectivity.rationale: Valet fetching scattered red cars from every aisle = scattered matches touching most heap pages; parked together = physically ordered table. Limit (pages must be read to know their contents) is accurate.

qp-composite-index-order.rationale: Phone book sorted by surname then first name = composite index; searching by first name only = non-leading column; checking each surname's Anitas = skip scan. Limit (a search per leading value, so few distinct leading values) is accurate.

qp-covering-partial-indexes.rationale: Library terminal answering without visiting shelves = index-only scan; 'check the shelves' mark = page not all-visible; VACUUM clears marks. Limit distinguishes staleness from snapshot visibility, which is the correct mechanism.

qp-expression-pattern-indexes.rationale: The neighbouring sargable lesson's dictionary analogy already covers expression indexes; repeating it would add nothing.

qp-index-maintenance.rationale: Costs list, catalog query and workflow; practical procedure where an analogy would be forced.

qp-sargable-predicates.rationale: Dictionary sorted by spelling cannot find words by third letter = index cannot search a transformed column; second dictionary = expression index. Limit is accurate.

qp-pagination-cursors.rationale: Counting pages from the front vs a bookmark = OFFSET vs keyset cursor. Limit (rows move between requests) is accurate.

qp-subquery-semantics.rationale: NULL semantics and plan differences are shown directly with executed SQL; an analogy risks blurring three-valued logic.

qp-query-round-trips.rationale: One drive per item = one round trip per query (N+1); whole list in one trip = batched query. Limit (very large batches still cost memory/transfer) is accurate.

qp-generic-plans-counts.rationale: Courier adopting a standard route after five big depot drops = generic plan chosen after five non-selective custom plans; village parcel = rare value. Matches plancache.c and my execution. Limit (no look at the new value unless invalidated or forced) is accurate.
